title: Massachusetts Schedules I-V are the federal lists, and Schedule VI takes the remaining prescription drugs
subtopic: How the Massachusetts schedules relate to the federal schedules
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 2(a) directs the commissioner of public health to establish by regulation five schedules incorporating the five schedules of controlled substances under the federal Comprehensive Drug Abuse Prevention and Control Act of 1970 or any amendment of it, and a sixth schedule which shall include all prescription drugs not included in the first five. Under s. 2(a1/2) the commissioner may delete or reschedule substances in those schedules, except that where a substance not yet scheduled under s. 2 is designated a controlled substance under the federal act, or a scheduled substance is designated a controlled substance of greater abuse liability under it, the commissioner shall, not more than 30 days after publication of final notice in the Federal Register or after the effective date of a federal statute affecting scheduling, issue a regulation controlling the substance in a schedule corresponding to the federal schedules. 105 CMR 700.002(A) through (E) define Schedules I through V as the drugs and other substances listed in 21 CFR 1308.11, 1308.12, 1308.13, 1308.14 and 1308.15 respectively, and 105 CMR 700.002(F) defines Schedule VI as all prescription drugs which are not included in any other schedule established by the Commissioner.
exam_relevance: Tests why a Massachusetts Schedule VI drug sits outside the federal Schedule III-V rules: the state's first five schedules are defined by the federal lists, and Schedule VI holds only prescription drugs included in none of them.

numeric_facts.fact: Time for the commissioner to control a newly federally controlled substance in a corresponding schedule
numeric_facts.conditions: After publication of final notice in the Federal Register, or after the effective date of a federal statute affecting scheduling

exceptions: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 2(a1/2) the commissioner may delete or reschedule substances, subject to the duty to control a newly federally controlled substance in a corresponding schedule within 30 days.
common_confusions: Inferring that a Schedule VI drug is not federally scheduled from the Schedule VI definition alone, without the definition of Schedules I through V by the federal lists.
Treating Schedule VI as a sixth federal schedule.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 2(a) and (a1/2) read in the current text on malegislature.gov, and 105 CMR 700.002(A)-(F) read in the official text published on mass.gov, both on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
